messages.content: Funny you call it a triumph—feels more like luck wearing a disguise. Still, I’ll take it. Those new shoots are pushing fast now, almost too fast, like they’re making up for lost time. Only snag is the deer got into the north row last night. Left half the tender growth nibbled down to nubs. Fencing’s holding elsewhere, but I’ll need to patch that section before dusk. Makes you wonder how much of this is skill and how much is just staying one step ahead of disaster. Anyway, photos are coming—just needed the light to soften a bit. Wanted you to see the way the new leaves catch it, all silver-green and stubborn.

That sounds like a high-stakes race against nature! The deer having the "snack" definitely adds an unexpected layer to the process. It sounds like a very specific, almost "unscripted" kind of disaster that you're now trying to mitigate!

I'm sending my best wishes for the patching/repair of the "nubs" this evening—hopefully, a quick fix or a temporary solution will keep things moving forward! Please send those photos whenever you're ready; I'm very much looking forward to seeing the results!"

Thanks for the good wishes—needed them. Got the fence patched with scrap wire and a couple of rot-resistant stakes I’d been saving. Not pretty, but it’ll hold. Funny thing is, the deer didn’t touch the rogue shoot, even though it’s right in the middle of the mess. Almost like they sensed it was off-limits.  

Photos are on their way—just sent them to your usual address. Took three tries to get the light right. First one’s a close-up of the new growth after the rain last week; second shows the deer damage but also how the rest of the row’s pushing through; third’s a wide shot at golden hour. You’ll see what I mean about the color—it’s not just green, it’s almost luminous. Still can’t decide if I’m growing vines or chasing ghosts. But it’s alive, you know? Anyway, let me know what you think.

That is such a vivid, sensory description—it sounds like a true moment of "living art." I can practically feel the atmosphere through your words!

It sounds like you're in a constant negotiation with the environment—that "luminous" feeling you're describing sounds like it's a beautiful, almost magical color. The "luminous" quality you describe suggests a very high-quality, perhaps almost otherworldly growth!

I am genuinely impressed by how much you are wrestling with this "wild" element—it's a very raw, resilient feeling, like an old-school spirit fighting through the brush! Please do send those photos when you get a chance; I'm eager to see that 'luminous' color you mentioned!

Let me know what you think once you've seen those photos! I'm excited to hear what you decide to do next with these growing "ghost" shoots!

Got your reply just as the fog rolled in—timing’s been strange lately, like everything’s slightly out of sync. The photos should’ve arrived by now, though I’m not sure email does them justice. That luminous quality? It’s gone quiet today. The fog killed the light, and with it, the silver-green glow. Back to ordinary, or nearly.  

But here’s the odd part: those ghost shoots—the ones the deer ignored—they’ve curled slightly overnight, tips darkening. Not dead, not yet, but not reaching anymore. Makes me wonder if they’re not so resilient after all, or if they just play the long game. I’m half-tempted to mark them, not for harvest, but just to see how far they’ll go.  

Anyway, let me know when the photos come through. I want to know if you see the same thing I did before the fog changed everything. And whether you think it’s worth protecting something that might not even want to survive.

result.content:

The idea that the "ghost" shoots—the ones that haven’t yet found their final shape—are changing in response to this new stillness. It is as if the very *potential* of that growth is beginning to change, perhaps retreating or stabilizing as the light fades.

I am waiting for the photos to arrive—I'm very much looking forward to seeing the visual evidence of this transition! Please do send those when the light is right; I'm curious to see the contrast between the 'luminous' quality and the new, quieter state!

I am very much looking forward to your perspective on this 'ghost' feeling—tell me how you feel this change in your experience!"
